I am 63 years old and have been farming these 16.1 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. I live alone, so I keep my management simple and practical. I know this land well. The soil is decent, and I have a well for irrigation, which is my lifeline on the North China Plain.

It is autumn now, and I am preparing to sow my winter wheat. I will plant the full 16.1 mu to wheat. I use an improved wheat variety that I have grown for several years — it is reliable, and I know how it behaves. Before sowing, I will do rotary tillage to prepare a good seedbed. For fertilizer, I will apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then topdress with urea in the spring. In total, I will put down about 14 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 2 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the wheat establish and store moisture, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. For pests and weeds, I will spray three times — herbicide, insecticide, and if the weather is damp, a fungicide. I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather cooperates.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize on the same 16.1 mu. I will use no-tillage sowing right after the wheat comes off — there is no time to waste in the summer season, and the soil moisture is precious. The hybrid maize seed gives good yields. I will apply about 16 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu, mostly as compound fertilizer at planting with a side-dressing of urea when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate twice — once if the early summer is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage when the crop needs it most. I will spray twice for pests and weeds. If the year is normal, I should get around 550 kg per mu from the maize.

I do not hire much labor because I work alone, so I keep my schedule tight and use machinery services for tillage, sowing, and harvest. I have learned that trying to cut corners on fertilizer or irrigation costs me more in lost yield at my age, so I stick to what works.
